questions.q: In 2003, the total population of a village was 3650, out of which 42% were females. In 2004, the total population increased by 10% as compared to the previous year. If the number of females remained the same in 2004, what was the percentage increase in the number of males in 2004 as compared to 2003 ?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: JSM/Deviation.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, logic laga! Agar population overall $10\%$ badhi hai aur females bilkul badhi nahi, toh jo total growth aayi hai wo *sirf* males ki wajah se aayi hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Growth value sidha nikal aur old males pe divide kar ke approximate kar. Mathematically :-

$\text{Total Inc} = 3650 \times 10\% = 365$

$\text{Old Males} = 3650 \times 58\% = 2117$

$\text{Male Inc } \% = \frac{365}{2117} \times 100$

$10\% = 211.7, 5\% = 105.8 \Rightarrow 15\% = 317.5$

$\text{Rem} \approx 47.5 \approx 2.2\% \Rightarrow 17.2\%$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Pura data calculate kar ekdum basic step se. Mathematically :-

$\text{Old Pop} = 3650 \Rightarrow F = 1533, M = 2117$

$\text{New Pop} = 4015 \Rightarrow F = 1533, M = 2482$

$\text{Inc in M} = 2482 - 2117 = 365$

$\% = \frac{365}{2117} \times 100 \approx 17.23\%$

Exam Takeaway: Absolute increase kis category me aa raha hai wo pehchan le, faltu exact multiply/divide me time kharab mat kar, options door door the.

questions.q: In a manufacturing unit, it was noted that the price of raw material has increased by $12.5\%$ and the labour cost has gone up from $25\%$ of the cost of raw material to $30\%$ of the NEW cost of raw material. By what percentage must the consumption of raw material be reduced to keep the total cost the same? (Approximate)
questions.s:
The "Pen-Free" Observation First:

Dekh bhai, $12.5\%$ ka fraction $\frac{1}{8}$ hota hai. Raw material 8 se 9 ho gaya. Purana labour 8 ka $25\%$ yani 2 tha. Naya labour 9 ka $30\%$ yani 2.7 hai. Purani total cost 10, nayi 11.7. Budget fix hai toh consumption theek cost ke ulte ratio me giregi (CPR).

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{RM (Old : New)} = 8 : 9 \\ \text{Labour (Old)} = 8 \times \frac{25}{100} = 2 \\ \text{Labour (New)} = 9 \times \frac{30}{100} = 2.7 \\ \text{Total Cost (Old : New)} = (8+2) : (9+2.7) = 10 : 11.7 = 100 : 117 \\ \text{Consumption Ratio} = 117 : 100 \\ \text{Percentage Reduction} = \frac{17}{117} \times 100 \approx 14.53\% $$

Exam Takeaway: Jab jeb mein paisa fixed ho (Budget = Constant), toh Price ratio ka ulta Consumption ratio hota hai. CPR is the ultimate tool!

questions.q: Everyday a fruit seller sells $75\%$ of his stock during the day and $20\%$ of his stock gets spoiled during the night. If in the morning of third day he had 128 fresh fruits, then how many fruits he had initially.
questions.s:
[Core Tool Triggered: Successive Change]

Pen-Free Observation: Day-Night milakar 1 din ka cycle poora hota hai. Morning of 3rd day matlab sirf 2 din poore hue hain (Day 1 aur Day 2).

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Din me $75\%$ becha $\Rightarrow$ bacha $25\%$ (yani $1/4$).
Raat me $20\%$ kharab $\Rightarrow$ bacha $80\%$ (yani $4/5$).
Roz ka bacha hua fraction $= \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{4}{5} = \frac{1}{5}$.
2 cycle ke baad bacha $= \text{Initial} \times \frac{1}{5} \times \frac{1}{5} = 128$.
Initial $= 128 \times 25 = 3200$.

Takeaway: Cycles ko dhyan se padhna, 'Morning of 3rd day' = End of 2nd day.

questions.q: A man started a business with a certain amount of capital. In the first year, he earned a 12.5% profit and donated 33.33% of the total capital (initial amount + profit). He followed the same procedure with the remaining capital after the second and the third year. If at the end of the three years, he is left with 82,944, what was the initial amount with which the man started his business ?
questions.s:
Tool Triggered: 2. Successive Change

The "Pen-Free" Observation First:
Dekh bhai, $12.5\%$ profit yani 9/8. Aur 33.33% donation yani bacha 2/3. Net saal ka factor: $9/8 \times 2/3 = 3/4$. Ye scene 3 saal chala. Yani Initial ko $(3/4)^3$ se multiply karenge toh 82944 aayega. 82944 ko $27/64$ se balance kar. Initial = $82944 \times 64 / 27$. Unit digit $4 \times 2 = 8$. Option me dekho sirf ek ke end me 8 hai. Boom!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Fractions + Unit digit match.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{Profit multiplier} = 1 + \frac{1}{8} = \frac{9}{8} \\ \text{Remaining multiplier} = 1 - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{2}{3} \\ \text{Yearly factor} = \frac{9}{8} \times \frac{2}{3} = \frac{3}{4} \\ I \times \left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^3 = 82944 \implies I \times \frac{27}{64} = 82944 \\ I = 82944 \times \frac{64}{27} \\ \text{End digit: } \frac{\dots 4}{27} \text{ gives end } 2. \text{ Then } 2 \times 4 = 8 \\ \implies \text{Ends with } 8 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Full breakdown calculation.

Mathematically :-
$$ I \times \frac{27}{64} = 82944 \\ \text{Divide by 9: } 82944 / 9 = 9216 \\ \text{Divide by 3: } 9216 / 3 = 3072 \\ I = 3072 \times 64 \\ 3072 \times 60 = 184320 \\ 3072 \times 4 = 12288 \\ I = 184320 + 12288 = 196608 $$

Exam Takeaway: Fractional successive jab bhi repeat ho, seedha cube or power laga aur last digit check kar.

questions.q: In a society 500 people are living $45\%$ play cricket, $29\%$ play hockey and $48\%$ play badminton, $18\%$ didn't any play game while $5\%$ people play all three games. If $6\%$ people play cricket and hockey both and $27\%$ play cricket and badminton both find the number of people who play only badminton?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 3. JSM / Deviation (Set Theory) Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, ye 3 wala diagrammatic set theory hai. Agar $18\%$ kuch nahi khelte, toh remaining $82\%$ kuch na kuch khel rahe hain. Seedha formula equate kar. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Formula pata hai na? $Total(A \cup B \cup C) = A + B + C - (A \cap B) - (B \cap C) - (A \cap C) + All(3)$. Yahan values daal: $82 = 45 + 29 + 48 - 6 - 27 - x + 5$. Solve kar: $82 = 127 - 33 - x + 5 \implies x = 127 - 28 - 82 = 17$? Check again: $82 = 94 - x \implies x = 12$. Yani Hockey & Badminton khelne wale $12\%$ hue. Ab chahiye 'Only Badminton'. Only Badminton $= B - (C \cap B) - (H \cap B) + All(3)$. Ye $+ All$ zaroori hai kyunki tune 5% ko do baar ghata diya intersect karne me. Toh $48 - 27 - 12 + 5 = 14\%$. Ab $500$ ka $14\%$ nikal de: $14 \times 5 = 70$. Shandaar calculation. Method 2 (Concept Builder): Venn Diagram bana, beech me 5 rakh. C & H = 6 tha, toh keval (C&H) = $6-5 = 1$. C & B = 27 tha, toh keval (C&B) = $27-5 = 22$. Ab bacha hua nikalega toh (H&B) ka only = 7 aayega. Badminton total 48 hai, toh Only B = $48 - (22 + 5 + 7) = 14\%$. Final count: $500 \times 0.14 = 70$. Dono se jawab mast aayega. Exam Takeaway: Only(C) nikalne ke liye hamesha formula $Total - Intersect1 - Intersect2 + All(3)$ laga diya kar, diagram se fast hai.

questions.q: A train's speed increases by $8.33\%$ at the first station, changes by x% at the second station, and decreases by $23.07\%$ at the third station. If the overall net change in the speed is an increase of $25\%$, find the value of x.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Multiplier.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, speed ki original value gayi bhaad me! Sirf percentages hain. 8.33% matlab 1/12 (multiplier 13/12), aur 23.07% matlab 3/13 drop (multiplier 10/13). 13 aur 13 mentally kat jayenge.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Chain Reaction Ratio.

Mathematically :-

$$ \frac{13}{12} \times t \times \frac{10}{13} = \frac{5}{4} \\ \frac{10}{12} \times t = \frac{5}{4} \\ \frac{5}{6} \times t = \frac{5}{4} \\ t = \frac{5}{4} \times \frac{6}{5} = \frac{3}{2} $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Value Assumption.

Mathematically :-

$$ 100 \times \frac{13}{12} \times t \times \frac{10}{13} = 125 \\ 100 \times \frac{10}{12} \times t = 125 \\ t = 1.5 \Rightarrow 50\% \text{ inc} $$

Exam Takeaway: Net effect hamesha intermediate factors ka direct multiple hota hai, object (train, machine ya population) matter nahi karta.

questions.q: A stationary supplier ordered 8 boxes of premium pens and some boxes of standard pens. The price of premium pens per box was twice that of standard pens. When the order was delivered, the number of boxes of premium and standard pens had been accidentally interchanged. This increased the total bill by 25%. What was the ratio of the original number of premium pens to the original number of boxes of standard pens? (CGL TIER I - 13/09/2025 - SHIFT 3)
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 4. Cross-Product Method

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, price ka ratio $P:S = 2:1$ given hai. Quantity $P=8$ aur $S=x$ hai. Interchange hone ki wajah se poora bill $25\%$ uchhal gaya. Yaha equations ko end tak lamba kheechna bewaqoofi hai, options ka sahara sabse badhiya shortcut hota hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Ek step ki equation bana aur cross-check ke liye sidha ratio nikal le!

Mathematically :-
$$\text{Orig Value} = 8(2) + x(1) = 16 + x$$
$$\text{New Value} = x(2) + 8(1) = 2x + 8$$
$$1.25(16 + x) = 2x + 8 \implies \frac{5}{4}(16 + x) = 2x + 8$$
$$80 + 5x = 8x + 32 \implies 3x = 48 \implies x = 16$$
$$\text{Ratio } P:S = 8:16 = 1:2$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Options se reverse check kar aur apna value bitha ke dekh le, seedha 15 second bachenge.

Mathematically :-
$$\text{Try Option } 1:2 \implies S = 16$$
$$\text{Orig} = 16+16=32, \ \text{New} = 32+8=40$$
$$\text{Increase} = \frac{8}{32} = 25\% \text{ (Condition Matched)}$$

Exam Takeaway: Interchange wale complex language problems me option plugging hamesha sabse tez aur khatarnak hathiyar hota hai.

questions.q: The average marks of the students in four subjects History, Biology, Chemistry and Physics together is 60%. The average marks of the students in History, Biology, Chemistry and Physics individually are 45%, 50%, 72% and 80% respectively. If the average marks of the students of History and Biology together is 48% and that of the students of Biology and Chemistry together is 60%. What is the ratio of number of students in History and Physics?
questions.s:
**Core Conceptual Tool:** 3. JSM (Junior Satisfaction Method) / Deviation

**Pen-Free Observation:** Dekh bhai, char groups hain, aur combination average (Alligation) ka double layer diya hai. Ratio nikalkar Deviation lagayega toh direct Physics ki value pop out karegi, bina lambe x-y multiplication ke.

**Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):** Pehle H(45) aur B(50) ko mix karke 48 la $\implies$ H:B ratio = $(50-48):(48-45) = 2:3$. Fir B(50) aur C(72) ko mix karke 60 la $\implies$ B:C ratio = $(72-60):(60-50) = 12:10 = 6:5$. H:B = 4:6 (double kiya taaki merge ho) toh H:B:C = 4:6:5. Total average 60 hai. Deviation base 60 rakh: H(-15) x 4 + B(-10) x 6 + C(+12) x 5 + P(+20) x X = 0. Solve kar: $-60 - 60 + 60 + 20X = 0 \implies 20X = 60 \implies X = 3$. Physics wale 3 hain. Ratio H:P = 4:3.

**Method 2 (Concept Builder):** Alligation se numbers ka weightage aata hai, aur Deviation us weightage ko balance karta hai. Agar manually total multiply karke add karta toh calculation teri jaan le leti. JSM is king!

**Exam Takeaway:** Jab multiple groups aur unke combined averages diye hon, Alligation aur JSM ka combo hamesha use karo taaki calculation single digit me rahe.

questions.q: There are 70 students in a class, but only 6/7 of them play at least one indoor game (Chess, Carrom, and Scrabble). It is given that 28.56% of the total students play Chess, 42.85% play Scrabble, and 57.14% play Carrom. Exactly 6 students play both Chess and Scrabble but not Carrom, 14.28% play both Scrabble and Carrom but not Chess, and 5 students play all 3 games. Find the number of students who play Chess and Carrom but not Scrabble.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Dekh bhai, saari percentages khatarnak dikh rahi hain par sab $\\frac{1}{7}$ ki family se hain! $14.28\\% = \\frac{1}{7}$, $28.56\\% = \\frac{2}{7}$, etc. Seedha total 70 par in fractions ko lagao aur exact integer values nikalo. Active bacche sirf $\\frac{6}{7} \\times 70 = 60$ hain.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Total active students (Union) = 60.
Ab direct values nikal out of total 70:
Chess (C) = $\\frac{2}{7} \\times 70 = 20$
Scrabble (S) = $\\frac{3}{7} \\times 70 = 30$
Carrom (M) = $\\frac{4}{7} \\times 70 = 40$
'Only C & S' = 6
'Only S & M' = $\\frac{1}{7} \\times 70 = 10$
'All 3' = 5
Hamein nikalna hai 'Only C & M', isko $x$ maan le.

Venn diagram ka sabse standard formula laga:
$$Union = n(C) + n(S) + n(M) - n(C \\cap S) - n(S \\cap M) - n(C \\cap M) + n(All)$$
Yahan overlaps mein 'Only 2' + 'All 3' aata hai.
$$60 = 20 + 30 + 40 - (6+5) - (10+5) - (x+5) + 5$$
$$60 = 90 - 11 - 15 - x - 5 + 5$$
$$60 = 64 - x \\implies x = 4$$
Seedha 4 aagaya! Option 2 is correct.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Venn diagram bana aur inner to outer region fill kar. Let 'Only C' = $c$, 'Only S' = $s$, 'Only M' = $m$.
Scrabble circle total is 30:
$$s + 6 + 10 + 5 = 30 \\implies s = 9$$
Chess circle total is 20:
$$c + 6 + 5 + x = 20 \\implies c + x = 9$$
Carrom circle total is 40:
$$m + 10 + 5 + x = 40 \\implies m + x = 25$$
Total Union = $c + s + m + 6 + 10 + x + 5 = 60$
Substitute $s = 9$:
$$c + m + x = 30$$
Hamein pata hai $c = 9 - x$ aur $m = 25 - x$. Isme put kar de:
$$(9 - x) + (25 - x) + x = 30$$
$$34 - x = 30 \\implies x = 4$$

Future Exam Takeaway:
SSC CGL Mains me aisi percentages hamesha fractional family se hoti hain. Pehchaan aur fraction me tod, phir standard set theory formula chipka de! Time bacha, rank la!

questions.q: 405 laptops are distributed in a corporate office in such a manner that the number of laptops that every department head gets is $20 \%$ of the total number of department heads. How many laptops does every department head get?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Total laptops 405 hain aur har kisi ko total logo ka $20 \%$ mil raha hai, matlab $1/5$. Seedha $5 \times 405$ ka square root nikalo total heads ke liye.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Total objects = (Number of people) $\times$ (Objects per person). Seedha fractional value ko multiply kar ke equation banao.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Let total heads} = N \\ \text{Laptops per head} = 20 \% \text{ of } N = \frac{N}{5} \\ \text{Total Laptops} = N \times \frac{N}{5} = 405 \\ N^2 = 2025 \implies N = 45 \\ \text{Per Head} = \frac{45}{5} = 9 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Variable assign karke step-by-step likho.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Let total heads be } x. \\ \text{Each gets } 0.2x \text{ laptops.} \\ x \times 0.2x = 405 \\ 0.2x^2 = 405 \implies x^2 = 2025 \\ x = 45 \\ \text{Laptops per head} = 0.2 \times 45 = 9 $$

Exam Takeaway: Aise cases me hamesha perfect square banta hai. Seedha denominator ko total se multiply kar ke root le lo.

Quick FormulaApplication
N = $\sqrt{Total \times Fraction\_Denom}$$\sqrt{405 \times 5} = 45$

questions.q: A man spends 80% of his income. His income has increased by 25%, but his expenditure remains the same. By what percent have his savings increased?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling / Basic Arithmetic

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Kharcha badha hi nahi! Yaani income me jo bhi extra paisa aaya, wo pura ka pura bachat (savings) me chala gaya. Direct logic.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai, Income = 100, Exp = 80, Sav = 20. Income ho gayi 125. Exp abhi bhi 80 hai. Toh new Savings = 45. Kitni badhi? 25. Original savings 20 thi. Percentage jump = $\frac{25}{20} \times 100 = 125\%$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): JSM se bhi soch sakta hai, par isme values itni choti aur simple hain ki basic direct equating is visually much faster.

Best Exam Approach: Sirf extra paise ka flow track kar. Extra 25 aaya aur wo direct 20 ki bachat par gaya. $25/20$ ka growth seedha 125% hai.

questions.q: A shopkeeper charges a sales tax of $x\%$ up to purchases of ₹2,000, and for amounts above it, he charges $y\%$. A customer pays a total tax of ₹320 when he purchases goods worth ₹6,000, and he pays a total tax of ₹680 for goods worth ₹12,000. The value of $(x - y)$ is:
questions.s:
The "Pen-Free" Observation First:

Dekh bhai, ₹6,000 aur ₹12,000 ke beech ka difference ₹6,000 hai. Ye extra ₹6,000 purntah $y\%$ slab (above ₹2,000) mein aayega. Tax difference = ₹680 - ₹320 = ₹360. Yani ₹6,000 ka $y\% = 360$. Sidha $y = 6$. Pehle case mein ₹6,000 pe 320 tax laga. ₹4,000 (above ₹2k) pe $6\%$ se ₹240 tax lag gaya. Bacha ₹80 tax ₹2,000 par laga hoga, yani $x = 4$. Toh $(x - y) = 4 - 6 = -2$.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Diff in Value} = 12000 - 6000 = 6000 \\ \text{Diff in Tax} = 680 - 320 = 360 \\ y\% \times 6000 = 360 \implies y = 6 \\ \text{Tax on upper 4000} = 4000 \times 6\% = 240 \\ \text{Tax on first 2000} = 320 - 240 = 80 \\ x\% \times 2000 = 80 \implies x = 4 \\ (x - y) = 4 - 6 = -2 $$

Exam Takeaway: Tax slab ke questions me humesha amounts aur tax ka direct difference nikalo. Solid Hacker mindset apna!

questions.q: If 45% of a number is 0.9 more than 30% of it, What is the number? (CGL TIER I - 14/09/2025-S2)
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai TestRipper, CGL ke aise lallu questions me toh pen pakdna bhi paap hai. Ek hi number hai, toh $45\%$ aur $30\%$ ka difference seedha $15\%$ bana. Ab $15\%$ ki value $0.9$ di hai. Seedha table count kar, $15 \times 6 = 90$, yaani 6 banega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Percentage difference ko seedha value se equate kar.

Mathematically :-
$$(45\% - 30\%) \ of \ N = 0.9 \\\\ 15\% \ of \ N = 0.9 \\\\ N = \frac{0.9}{15} \times 100 = \frac{90}{15} = 6$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Variable $N$ rakh ke fractions likho.

Mathematically :-
$$0.45N - 0.30N = 0.9 \\\\ 0.15N = 0.9 \\\\ N = \frac{0.9}{0.15} = 6$$

Exam Takeaway: Difference hamesha directly equate hota hai agar base number ek hi ho.

questions.q: A stock portfolio consists of four stocks. Stock A represents 10% of the portfolio and has a return of 4%. Stock B represents 20% of the portfolio and has a return of 8%. Stock C represents 30% of the portfolio and has a return of 3%. Stock D represents the remaining 40% of the portfolio and has a <u>negative-return</u> of 6%. What is the average return of the portfolio?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 3. JSM/Deviation

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, yahan portfolio ke alag alag hisso ko unke returns se seedha multiply karna hai. Positive wale add honge aur jisme nuksan (negative) hai wo subtract hoga. Aur total base humesha $100\%$ ka weight rahega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Weights aur returns ki values ko direct multiply karke jodd de aur seedha $100$ se divide maar!

Mathematically :-
$$10(4) + 20(8) + 30(3) + 40(-6) = 40 + 160 + 90 - 240 = 50$$
$$\text{Avg Return} = \frac{50}{100} = 0.5\%$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Standard weighted average ka proper formula laga ke calculation kar.

Mathematically :-
$$\frac{w_1r_1 + w_2r_2 + w_3r_3 + w_4r_4}{w_1+w_2+w_3+w_4} = \frac{40+160+90-240}{100} = 0.5\%$$

Exam Takeaway: Weighted average nikalte waqt negative values pe dhyan se nazar rakhna, wahan silly mistake ke chances bahut zyada hote hain.

questions.q: A mixture contains $60\%$ milk. If 20 liters of water is added to the 80-liter mixture, what is the new percentage of milk? (CGL TIER I - $\frac{22}{09}$/2025 - SHIFT 3)
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, mixture me paani daloge toh paani badlega, lekin milk ki absolute amount constant rahegi. Wahi nikal ke naye base par percentage bana de.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Constant element tracking. Mathematically :-
$$Milk = 80 \times 0.60 = 48$$
$$New\_Total = 80 + 20 = 100$$
$$\% = \frac{48}{100} \times 100 = 48\%$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Fractional proportion. Mathematically :-
$$Milk = \frac{3}{5} \times 80 = 48$$
$$Water = \frac{2}{5} \times 80 = 32$$
$$New\_Water = 32 + 20 = 52$$
$$\% = \frac{48}{48+52} \times 100 = 48\%$$

Exam Takeaway: Mixture me jo element intact rahe usi absolute value ko total target par naya percentage banane ke liye use kar.

questions.q: A number was mistakenly increased by 25% instead of decreased by 20%. By what percent is the final result more than the correct value?
questions.s:
**Core Conceptual Tool:** 5. Unitary Scaling

**Pen-Free Observation:** Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Mistake walo sawalon me hamesha BASE (denominator) us value ko banana hota hai jo 'Sahih' (correct) thi. Original number ko 100 maan, sahi result aur galat result dono nikal.

**Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):** Base 100 liya. Sahi kaam = 20\% ghatana tha, yani aana chahiye tha 80. Galat kaam = 25\% badha diya, yani le aya 125. Pucha hai final result (125) sahi (80) se kitna percent jyada hai. Value me jyada hai $125 - 80 = 45$. Base sahi value (80) rakh: $\frac{45}{80} \times 100 = \frac{9}{16} \times 100$. $\frac{1}{16}$ hota hai $6.25\%$, toh $9 \times 6.25 = 56.25\%$.

**Method 2 (Concept Builder):** Ratio method bhi op hai. Sahi value 80, galat 125. Ratio ban gaya $80:125 = 16:25$. Increase hai 9 units ka 16 par. Standard fraction $\frac{9}{16}$ aa gaya seedha!

**Exam Takeaway:** "More than the correct value" likha hai matlab percentage error original number (100) par nahi, balki 'Correct Outcome' (80) par nikalni padegi.

questions.q: A man's annual income has increased by 5000 but the tax on income that he has to pay has reduced from 15% to 12%. While in both the situations, 30% of the income tax is tax-free. Find the initial income, if equal tax is paid in both cases?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: CPR (Constant Product Ratio)

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Tax = Income $\times$ Tax Rate. Jab Tax (Product) constant hai, toh Income aur Tax Rate inversely proportional honge. Rate 15 se 12 hua (Ratio 5:4). Toh Income 4 se 5 hui hogi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Tax free portion (30%) dono taraf cut jayega, ignore kar. Tax rate ratio = 15:12 = 5:4. CPR lagao: Tax same hai toh Income ratio = 4:5. Gap 1 unit ka hai. 1 unit = 5000 (increase). Toh initial income 4 units = 20000. Pen nahi uthana tha isme!

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Equation: $70\% \text{ of } 15\% \text{ of } x = 70\% \text{ of } 12\% \text{ of } (x + 5000)$. $15x = 12x + 60000 \implies 3x = 60000 \implies x = 20000$.

Future Exam Takeaway: CPR method CGL Mains me aag laga dega! Product constant dekhte hi cross-ratio lagao.

questions.q: Entry ticket of a cinema hall is 120 when the price is reduced by a certain percentage then the sales of ticket increases by 37.5%. whereas the overall collection is reduced by 25%. Find the percentage decrease in the price of ticket ?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Cross-Product

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, ye basic equation hai $Price \times Sales = Collection$. Yaha ₹120 kisi kaam ka nahi hai kyuki result me percentage pucha hai. Collection ka aur Sales ka ratio banega, aur directly divide karke Price ka ratio niklega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Dependent variable (Collection) ko independent variables (Sales) se divide kar, Price nikal.

Mathematically :-
$$P = \frac{Collection}{Sales} \\\\ P_{ratio} = \frac{C_1}{S_1} : \frac{C_2}{S_2} = \frac{4}{8} : \frac{3}{11} = \frac{1}{2} : \frac{3}{11} \\\\ Cross \ Multiply \Rightarrow 11 : 6 \\\\ \% \ Decrease = \frac{11 - 6}{11} \times 100 = \frac{5}{11} \times 100 = 45.45\%$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Actual ₹120 le kar math solve kar, end me percent nikalo.

Mathematically :-
$$P_1 = 120, S_1 = 8x \Rightarrow C_1 = 960x \\\\ C_2 = 960x \times 0.75 = 720x \\\\ S_2 = 8x \times 1.375 = 11x \\\\ P_2 = \frac{720x}{11x} \approx 65.45 \\\\ \% \ Decrease = \frac{120 - 65.45}{120} \times 100 = 45.45\%$$

Exam Takeaway: Absolute values are completely useless if the question asks for a percentage output. Ignore them.

Multiplier EffectDivide final ratio by one shift ratio to get the other shift ratio.

questions.q: x is inversely proportional to y. If x is increased by $37.5\%$ then find % change in the value of y?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 1. CPR (Constant Product Ratio)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, $x$ aur $y$ inversely proportional hain, iska matlab unka product $x \times y = K$ constant hai. Direct CPR shift lagega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): $37.5\%$ ki fraction $3/8$ hoti hai. X me increase hua $+3/8$. Toh CPR shift me Y decrease hoga $-3/(8+3) = -3/11$. $1/11$ hota hai $9.09\%$, toh $3/11$ banega $27.27\%$. Aankhon hi aankhon me answer!

Mathematically :-
$X_{inc} = +\frac{3}{8}$
$Y_{dec} = -\frac{3}{11}$
$\% = \frac{3}{11} \times 100 = 27.27\%$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Ratio se dekh le. $x$ agar 8 se 11 hua, toh inverse relation me $y$ 11 se 8 hoga. 3 ghata 11 par. Baakhi kahani same hai.

Mathematically :-
$xy = k$
$X_{new} = \frac{11}{8}x$
$Y_{new} = \frac{k}{\frac{11}{8}x} = \frac{8}{11}y$
$\text{Dec} = y - \frac{8}{11}y = \frac{3}{11}y$
$\% = \frac{3}{11} \times 100 = 27.27\%$

Exam Takeaway: Inversely proportional bolne ka matlab hi CPR lagana hai, fractions yaad hone chahiye tips par.

Y (Decrease)$-3/11$

questions.q: If a number is first increased by 15%, then reduced by 15%, it results in 782. If the same number is first reduced by 25%, then increased by 25% and again reduced by 20%, then what will be the resulting number?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, same percentage increase/decrease hamesha $(x^2/100)\%$ ka loss deta hai. $15\%$ se $2.25\%$ loss yani 97.75% of number 782 hai. Decimal adjust kar number 800 aaya. Fir aage seedha fractions ko chain me kaat de.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): First setup se number extract kar aur second me purely fractions apply kar.

Mathematically :-
$$Loss = \frac{15^2}{100} = 2.25\% \\\\ 97.75\% \ of \ N = 782 \Rightarrow N = 800 \\\\ Final = 800 \times \frac{3}{4} \times \frac{5}{4} \times \frac{4}{5} \\\\ Final = 800 \times \frac{3}{4} = 600$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Decimal chain ko har step par equate kar.

Mathematically :-
$$N \times 1.15 \times 0.85 = 782 \\\\ N = \frac{782}{0.9775} = 800 \\\\ Ans = 800 \times 0.75 \times 1.25 \times 0.80 \\\\ Ans = 600 \times 1.25 \times 0.80 = 600$$

Exam Takeaway: Chain rule me fractions last tak cancel hone ke liye wait karti hain, intermediate gunna-bhag me time waste na karo.

Constant Change Rule$+A\%, -A\% \Rightarrow Net \ Loss \ (A^2/100)\%$

questions.q: The salary of a person is ₹30,000. It increases first by $2k\%$ and then again by $k\%$, making his new salary ₹44,850. If his original salary was instead decreased by $2k\%$ and then further decreased by $k\%$, what would his new salary be?
questions.s:
The "Pen-Free" Observation First:

Dekh bhai, Final / Initial = $\frac{44850}{30000} = 1.495$. Matlab lagbhag $50\%$ ka growth hua hai successive me. Equation mat bana, Hit and trial best hai. $k=15$ lo, toh $+30\%$ aur $+15\%$ ka net lagbhag $49.5\%$ fit baith gaya!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Net Increase} = \frac{44850 - 30000}{30000} = 49.5\% \\ 2k + k + \frac{2k^2}{100} = 49.5 \implies k = 15 \text{ (by Observation)} \\ \text{Decrease } 1 = 30000 \times (1 - 0.30) = 21000 \\ \text{Decrease } 2 = 21000 \times (1 - 0.15) = 17850 $$

Exam Takeaway: Successive increase/decrease me agar exact formula lagane bethe toh quadratic banegi. Smart assumption + Hit & Trial rules the exam!

questions.q: In the year 2014, the population of a city was 30,000. The population of the city increased in 2015, 2016 and 2017 by a constant number. In the year 2018, if the population of the city was increased by 20% over the previous year then the population of the city become 27600 more than that of the year 2014. What is the ratio of the percentage increase in the population of the city over the previous year in the year 2015 to that in the year 2017 over the previous year?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, "constant number" matlab AP chal rahi hai. 2018 ki population $2014 + 27600$ se aayegi, phir $20\%$ back karke 2017 ka pata chalega. Reverse calculations kar mentally.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Reverse series laga aur yearly increase nikal. Mathematically :-

$P_{2018} = 30000 + 27600 = 57600$

$P_{2017} = \frac{57600}{1.2} = 48000$

$\text{Inc in 3 yrs} = 48000 - 30000 = 18000 \Rightarrow \text{6000 per yr}$

$\%_{2015} = \frac{6000}{30000} = \frac{1}{5}$

$\%_{2017} = \frac{6000}{42000} = \frac{1}{7}$

$\text{Ratio} = \frac{1}{5} : \frac{1}{7} = 7 : 5$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Variables assume karke AP ka formula chalao. Mathematically :-

$P_{2014} = 30000$

$P_{2017} = 30000 + 3d$

$(30000 + 3d) \times 1.2 = 57600$

$30000 + 3d = 48000 \Rightarrow 3d = 18000 \Rightarrow d = 6000$

$\frac{6000}{30000} : \frac{6000}{30000+2(6000)} = \frac{1}{5} : \frac{1}{7} = 7:5$

Exam Takeaway: Constant increase humesha Arithmetic Progression (AP) hota hai, pichhe se backward aana smart move hai.

AP Logic$\text{Value} = a + (n-1)d$

questions_hin.q_hi: In a manufacturing unit, it was noted that the price of raw material has increased by $12.5\%$ and the labour cost has gone up from $25\%$ of the cost of raw material to $30\%$ of the NEW cost of raw material. By what percentage must the consumption of raw material be reduced to keep the total cost the same? (Approximate)
questions_hin.s_hi:
The "Pen-Free" Observation First:

Dekh bhai, $12.5\%$ ka fraction $\frac{1}{8}$ hota hai. Raw material 8 se 9 ho gaya. Purana labour 8 ka $25\%$ yani 2 tha. Naya labour 9 ka $30\%$ yani 2.7 hai. Purani total cost 10, nayi 11.7. Budget fix hai toh consumption theek cost ke ulte ratio me giregi (CPR).

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{RM (Old : New)} = 8 : 9 \\ \text{Labour (Old)} = 8 \times \frac{25}{100} = 2 \\ \text{Labour (New)} = 9 \times \frac{30}{100} = 2.7 \\ \text{Total Cost (Old : New)} = (8+2) : (9+2.7) = 10 : 11.7 = 100 : 117 \\ \text{Consumption Ratio} = 117 : 100 \\ \text{Percentage Reduction} = \frac{17}{117} \times 100 \approx 14.53\% $$

Exam Takeaway: Jab jeb mein paisa fixed ho (Budget = Constant), toh Price ratio ka ulta Consumption ratio hota hai. CPR is the ultimate tool!

questions_hin.q_hi: Everyday a fruit seller sells $75\%$ of his stock during the day and $20\%$ of his stock gets spoiled during the night. If in the morning of third day he had 128 fresh fruits, then how many fruits he had initially.
questions_hin.s_hi:
[Core Tool Triggered: Successive Change]

Pen-Free Observation: Day-Night milakar 1 din ka cycle poora hota hai. Morning of 3rd day matlab sirf 2 din poore hue hain (Day 1 aur Day 2).

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Din me $75\%$ becha $\Rightarrow$ bacha $25\%$ (yani $1/4$).
Raat me $20\%$ kharab $\Rightarrow$ bacha $80\%$ (yani $4/5$).
Roz ka bacha hua fraction $= \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{4}{5} = \frac{1}{5}$.
2 cycle ke baad bacha $= \text{Initial} \times \frac{1}{5} \times \frac{1}{5} = 128$.
Initial $= 128 \times 25 = 3200$.

Takeaway: Cycles ko dhyan se padhna, 'Morning of 3rd day' = End of 2nd day.

questions_hin.q_hi: A man started a business with a certain amount of capital. In the first year, he earned a 12.5% profit and donated 33.33% of the total capital (initial amount + profit). He followed the same procedure with the remaining capital after the second and the third year. If at the end of the three years, he is left with 82,944, what was the initial amount with which the man started his business ?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Tool Triggered: 2. Successive Change

The "Pen-Free" Observation First:
Dekh bhai, $12.5\%$ profit yani 9/8. Aur 33.33% donation yani bacha 2/3. Net saal ka factor: $9/8 \times 2/3 = 3/4$. Ye scene 3 saal chala. Yani Initial ko $(3/4)^3$ se multiply karenge toh 82944 aayega. 82944 ko $27/64$ se balance kar. Initial = $82944 \times 64 / 27$. Unit digit $4 \times 2 = 8$. Option me dekho sirf ek ke end me 8 hai. Boom!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Fractions + Unit digit match.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{Profit multiplier} = 1 + \frac{1}{8} = \frac{9}{8} \\ \text{Remaining multiplier} = 1 - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{2}{3} \\ \text{Yearly factor} = \frac{9}{8} \times \frac{2}{3} = \frac{3}{4} \\ I \times \left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^3 = 82944 \implies I \times \frac{27}{64} = 82944 \\ I = 82944 \times \frac{64}{27} \\ \text{End digit: } \frac{\dots 4}{27} \text{ gives end } 2. \text{ Then } 2 \times 4 = 8 \\ \implies \text{Ends with } 8 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Full breakdown calculation.

Mathematically :-
$$ I \times \frac{27}{64} = 82944 \\ \text{Divide by 9: } 82944 / 9 = 9216 \\ \text{Divide by 3: } 9216 / 3 = 3072 \\ I = 3072 \times 64 \\ 3072 \times 60 = 184320 \\ 3072 \times 4 = 12288 \\ I = 184320 + 12288 = 196608 $$

Exam Takeaway: Fractional successive jab bhi repeat ho, seedha cube or power laga aur last digit check kar.

questions_hin.q_hi: In a society 500 people are living $45\%$ play cricket, $29\%$ play hockey and $48\%$ play badminton, $18\%$ didn't any play game while $5\%$ people play all three games. If $6\%$ people play cricket and hockey both and $27\%$ play cricket and badminton both find the number of people who play only badminton?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: 3. JSM / Deviation (Set Theory) Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, ye 3 wala diagrammatic set theory hai. Agar $18\%$ kuch nahi khelte, toh remaining $82\%$ kuch na kuch khel rahe hain. Seedha formula equate kar. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Formula pata hai na? $Total(A \cup B \cup C) = A + B + C - (A \cap B) - (B \cap C) - (A \cap C) + All(3)$. Yahan values daal: $82 = 45 + 29 + 48 - 6 - 27 - x + 5$. Solve kar: $82 = 127 - 33 - x + 5 \implies x = 127 - 28 - 82 = 17$? Check again: $82 = 94 - x \implies x = 12$. Yani Hockey & Badminton khelne wale $12\%$ hue. Ab chahiye 'Only Badminton'. Only Badminton $= B - (C \cap B) - (H \cap B) + All(3)$. Ye $+ All$ zaroori hai kyunki tune 5% ko do baar ghata diya intersect karne me. Toh $48 - 27 - 12 + 5 = 14\%$. Ab $500$ ka $14\%$ nikal de: $14 \times 5 = 70$. Shandaar calculation. Method 2 (Concept Builder): Venn Diagram bana, beech me 5 rakh. C & H = 6 tha, toh keval (C&H) = $6-5 = 1$. C & B = 27 tha, toh keval (C&B) = $27-5 = 22$. Ab bacha hua nikalega toh (H&B) ka only = 7 aayega. Badminton total 48 hai, toh Only B = $48 - (22 + 5 + 7) = 14\%$. Final count: $500 \times 0.14 = 70$. Dono se jawab mast aayega. Exam Takeaway: Only(C) nikalne ke liye hamesha formula $Total - Intersect1 - Intersect2 + All(3)$ laga diya kar, diagram se fast hai.

1. Badminton Total$48\%$

The average marks of the students in History, Biology, Chemistry and Physics individually are 45%, 50%, 72% and 80% respectively. If the average marks of the students of History and Biology together is 48% and that of the students of Biology and Chemistry together is 60%. **Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):** Pehle H(45) aur B(50) ko mix karke 48 la $\implies$ H:B ratio = $(50-48):(48-45) = 2:3$. Fir B(50) aur C(72) ko mix karke 60 la $\implies$ B:C ratio = $(72-60):(60-50) = 12:10 = 6:5$. H:B = 4:6 (double kiya taaki merge ho) toh H:B:C = 4:6:5. Total average 60 hai. **Method 2 (Concept Builder):** Alligation se numbers ka weightage aata hai, aur Deviation us weightage ko balance karta hai. Agar manually total multiply karke add karta toh calculation teri jaan le leti. JSM is king!

**Exam Takeaway:** Jab multiple groups aur unke combined averages diye hon, Alligation aur JSM ka combo hamesha use karo taaki calculation single digit me rahe.

questions_hin.q_hi: There are 70 students in a class, but only 6/7 of them play at least one indoor game (Chess, Carrom, and Scrabble). It is given that 28.56% of the total students play Chess, 42.85% play Scrabble, and 57.14% play Carrom. Exactly 6 students play both Chess and Scrabble but not Carrom, 14.28% play both Scrabble and Carrom but not Chess, and 5 students play all 3 games. Find the number of students who play Chess and Carrom but not Scrabble.
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Dekh bhai, saari percentages khatarnak dikh rahi hain par sab $\\frac{1}{7}$ ki family se hain! $14.28\\% = \\frac{1}{7}$, $28.56\\% = \\frac{2}{7}$, etc. Seedha total 70 par in fractions ko lagao aur exact integer values nikalo. Active bacche sirf $\\frac{6}{7} \\times 70 = 60$ hain.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Total active students (Union) = 60.
Ab direct values nikal out of total 70:
Chess (C) = $\\frac{2}{7} \\times 70 = 20$
Scrabble (S) = $\\frac{3}{7} \\times 70 = 30$
Carrom (M) = $\\frac{4}{7} \\times 70 = 40$
'Only C & S' = 6
'Only S & M' = $\\frac{1}{7} \\times 70 = 10$
'All 3' = 5
Hamein nikalna hai 'Only C & M', isko $x$ maan le.

Venn diagram ka sabse standard formula laga:
$$Union = n(C) + n(S) + n(M) - n(C \\cap S) - n(S \\cap M) - n(C \\cap M) + n(All)$$
Yahan overlaps mein 'Only 2' + 'All 3' aata hai.
$$60 = 20 + 30 + 40 - (6+5) - (10+5) - (x+5) + 5$$
$$60 = 90 - 11 - 15 - x - 5 + 5$$
$$60 = 64 - x \\implies x = 4$$
Seedha 4 aagaya! Option 2 is correct.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Venn diagram bana aur inner to outer region fill kar. Let 'Only C' = $c$, 'Only S' = $s$, 'Only M' = $m$.
Scrabble circle total is 30:
$$s + 6 + 10 + 5 = 30 \\implies s = 9$$
Chess circle total is 20:
$$c + 6 + 5 + x = 20 \\implies c + x = 9$$
Carrom circle total is 40:
$$m + 10 + 5 + x = 40 \\implies m + x = 25$$
Total Union = $c + s + m + 6 + 10 + x + 5 = 60$
Substitute $s = 9$:
$$c + m + x = 30$$
Hamein pata hai $c = 9 - x$ aur $m = 25 - x$. Isme put kar de:
$$(9 - x) + (25 - x) + x = 30$$
$$34 - x = 30 \\implies x = 4$$

Future Exam Takeaway:
SSC CGL Mains me aisi percentages hamesha fractional family se hoti hain. Pehchaan aur fraction me tod, phir standard set theory formula chipka de! Time bacha, rank la!

questions_hin.q_hi: 405 laptops are distributed in a corporate office in such a manner that the number of laptops that every department head gets is $20 \%$ of the total number of department heads. How many laptops does every department head get?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Total laptops 405 hain aur har kisi ko total logo ka $20 \%$ mil raha hai, matlab $1/5$. Seedha $5 \times 405$ ka square root nikalo total heads ke liye.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Total objects = (Number of people) $\times$ (Objects per person). Seedha fractional value ko multiply kar ke equation banao.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Let total heads} = N \\ \text{Laptops per head} = 20 \% \text{ of } N = \frac{N}{5} \\ \text{Total Laptops} = N \times \frac{N}{5} = 405 \\ N^2 = 2025 \implies N = 45 \\ \text{Per Head} = \frac{45}{5} = 9 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Variable assign karke step-by-step likho.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Let total heads be } x. \\ \text{Each gets } 0.2x \text{ laptops.} \\ x \times 0.2x = 405 \\ 0.2x^2 = 405 \implies x^2 = 2025 \\ x = 45 \\ \text{Laptops per head} = 0.2 \times 45 = 9 $$

Exam Takeaway: Aise cases me hamesha perfect square banta hai. Seedha denominator ko total se multiply kar ke root le lo.

Quick FormulaApplication
N = $\sqrt{Total \times Fraction\_Denom}$$\sqrt{405 \times 5} = 45$

questions_hin.q_hi: A man spends 80% of his income. His income has increased by 25%, but his expenditure remains the same. By what percent have his savings increased?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling / Basic Arithmetic

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Kharcha badha hi nahi! Yaani income me jo bhi extra paisa aaya, wo pura ka pura bachat (savings) me chala gaya. Direct logic.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai, Income = 100, Exp = 80, Sav = 20. Income ho gayi 125. Exp abhi bhi 80 hai. Toh new Savings = 45. Kitni badhi? 25. Original savings 20 thi. Percentage jump = $\frac{25}{20} \times 100 = 125\%$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): JSM se bhi soch sakta hai, par isme values itni choti aur simple hain ki basic direct equating is visually much faster.

Best Exam Approach: Sirf extra paise ka flow track kar. Extra 25 aaya aur wo direct 20 ki bachat par gaya. $25/20$ ka growth seedha 125% hai.

questions_hin.q_hi: A shopkeeper charges a sales tax of $x\%$ up to purchases of ₹2,000, and for amounts above it, he charges $y\%$. A customer pays a total tax of ₹320 when he purchases goods worth ₹6,000, and he pays a total tax of ₹680 for goods worth ₹12,000. The value of $(x - y)$ is:
questions_hin.s_hi:
The "Pen-Free" Observation First:

Dekh bhai, ₹6,000 aur ₹12,000 ke beech ka difference ₹6,000 hai. Ye extra ₹6,000 purntah $y\%$ slab (above ₹2,000) mein aayega. Tax difference = ₹680 - ₹320 = ₹360. Yani ₹6,000 ka $y\% = 360$. Sidha $y = 6$. Pehle case mein ₹6,000 pe 320 tax laga. ₹4,000 (above ₹2k) pe $6\%$ se ₹240 tax lag gaya. Bacha ₹80 tax ₹2,000 par laga hoga, yani $x = 4$. Toh $(x - y) = 4 - 6 = -2$.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Diff in Value} = 12000 - 6000 = 6000 \\ \text{Diff in Tax} = 680 - 320 = 360 \\ y\% \times 6000 = 360 \implies y = 6 \\ \text{Tax on upper 4000} = 4000 \times 6\% = 240 \\ \text{Tax on first 2000} = 320 - 240 = 80 \\ x\% \times 2000 = 80 \implies x = 4 \\ (x - y) = 4 - 6 = -2 $$

Exam Takeaway: Tax slab ke questions me humesha amounts aur tax ka direct difference nikalo. Solid Hacker mindset apna!

questions_hin.q_hi: A solid metallic sphere of radius R is heated so that its radius increases by 10%. Find the approximate percentage increase in its volume. (CHSL TIER I - 25/11/2025 - SHIFT 3)
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: 2. Successive Change (The Chain Reaction)

Pen-Free Observation: Sphere ki volume radius ke cube ($r^3$) par depend hoti hai. 10% ka multiplier 1.1 hota hai, toh volume multiplier $1.1^3 = 1.331$ aayega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai TestRipper, radius 1D hai aur Volume 3D me hai. Increment $10\% = \frac{1}{10}$. Toh multiplier hua $\frac{11}{10}$.
Volume ka ratio nikalo: $(\frac{11}{10})^3 = \frac{1331}{1000}$.
Base 1000 se value 1331 ho gayi. Increment = 331. Base 100 par karega toh $= 33.1\%$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Bohot log isme bas roughly $3 \times 10 = 30\%$, bol dete hain, par exactly calculate ($1.331$) karna hi thik rehta hai precision options ko clear karne ke liye.

Exam Takeaway: Bhai tu SSC ki tayari kar raha hai, cubes 15 tak tere dimaag me chhape hone chahiye. $11^3 = 1331$ toh sabse common hai.

questions_hin.q_hi: Some students (only boys and girls) from different schools appeared for an Olympiad exam. $40\%$ of the boys and $25\%$ of the girls failed the exam. The number of boys who passed the exam was 30 more than that of the girls who passed the exam. A total of 170 students failed. Find the number of students that appeared for the exam?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, fail ki value total di hai, pass ki relative difference di hai. Do equations, do variable ka classical case hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Failed wali equation likh: $0.4B + 0.25G = 170$. Passed wali equation: $0.6B - 0.75G = 30$. Pehli equation me $3$ ka multiply maar de taki G barabar ho jaye: $1.2B + 0.75G = 510$. Ab isme passed wali jodd de, $+0.75G$ aur $-0.75G$ kat jayenge. Method 2 (Concept Builder): Options se check karna ninja tactic hai. Agar total 500 ho, toh B=300 aur G=200 pe fit baithta hai kya dekh lo. Fail B=120, Fail G=50. Total fail 170 (Match!). Pass B=180, Pass G=150. Difference 30 (Match!). Option hi best hai bhai!

questions_hin.q_hi: If 45% of a number is 0.9 more than 30% of it, What is the number? (CGL TIER I - 14/09/2025-S2)
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai TestRipper, CGL ke aise lallu questions me toh pen pakdna bhi paap hai. Ek hi number hai, toh $45\%$ aur $30\%$ ka difference seedha $15\%$ bana. Ab $15\%$ ki value $0.9$ di hai. Seedha table count kar, $15 \times 6 = 90$, yaani 6 banega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Percentage difference ko seedha value se equate kar.

Mathematically :-
$$(45\% - 30\%) \ of \ N = 0.9 \\\\ 15\% \ of \ N = 0.9 \\\\ N = \frac{0.9}{15} \times 100 = \frac{90}{15} = 6$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Variable $N$ rakh ke fractions likho.

Mathematically :-
$$0.45N - 0.30N = 0.9 \\\\ 0.15N = 0.9 \\\\ N = \frac{0.9}{0.15} = 6$$

Exam Takeaway: Difference hamesha directly equate hota hai agar base number ek hi ho.

questions_hin.q_hi: A stock portfolio consists of four stocks. Stock A represents 10% of the portfolio and has a return of 4%. Stock B represents 20% of the portfolio and has a return of 8%. Stock C represents 30% of the portfolio and has a return of 3%. Stock D represents the remaining 40% of the portfolio and has a <u>negative-return</u> of 6%. What is the average return of the portfolio?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: 3. JSM/Deviation

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, yahan portfolio ke alag alag hisso ko unke returns se seedha multiply karna hai. Positive wale add honge aur jisme nuksan (negative) hai wo subtract hoga. Aur total base humesha $100\%$ ka weight rahega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Weights aur returns ki values ko direct multiply karke jodd de aur seedha $100$ se divide maar!

Mathematically :-
$$10(4) + 20(8) + 30(3) + 40(-6) = 40 + 160 + 90 - 240 = 50$$
$$\text{Avg Return} = \frac{50}{100} = 0.5\%$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Standard weighted average ka proper formula laga ke calculation kar.

Mathematically :-
$$\frac{w_1r_1 + w_2r_2 + w_3r_3 + w_4r_4}{w_1+w_2+w_3+w_4} = \frac{40+160+90-240}{100} = 0.5\%$$

Exam Takeaway: Weighted average nikalte waqt negative values pe dhyan se nazar rakhna, wahan silly mistake ke chances bahut zyada hote hain.

List IList II
Weighted Sum$\frac{\Sigma (Weight \times Return)}{\Sigma Weight}$

questions_hin.q_hi: A mixture contains $60\%$ milk. If 20 liters of water is added to the 80-liter mixture, what is the new percentage of milk? (CGL TIER I - $\frac{22}{09}$/2025 - SHIFT 3)
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, mixture me paani daloge toh paani badlega, lekin milk ki absolute amount constant rahegi. Wahi nikal ke naye base par percentage bana de.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Constant element tracking. Mathematically :-
$$Milk = 80 \times 0.60 = 48$$
$$New\_Total = 80 + 20 = 100$$
$$\% = \frac{48}{100} \times 100 = 48\%$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Fractional proportion. Mathematically :-
$$Milk = \frac{3}{5} \times 80 = 48$$
$$Water = \frac{2}{5} \times 80 = 32$$
$$New\_Water = 32 + 20 = 52$$
$$\% = \frac{48}{48+52} \times 100 = 48\%$$

Exam Takeaway: Mixture me jo element intact rahe usi absolute value ko total target par naya percentage banane ke liye use kar.

Constant AnchorNever track the changing element, track what remains unchanged.

questions_hin.q_hi: A number was mistakenly increased by 25% instead of decreased by 20%. By what percent is the final result more than the correct value?
questions_hin.s_hi:
**Core Conceptual Tool:** 5. Unitary Scaling

**Pen-Free Observation:** Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Mistake walo sawalon me hamesha BASE (denominator) us value ko banana hota hai jo 'Sahih' (correct) thi. Original number ko 100 maan, sahi result aur galat result dono nikal.

**Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):** Base 100 liya. Sahi kaam = 20\% ghatana tha, yani aana chahiye tha 80. Galat kaam = 25\% badha diya, yani le aya 125. Pucha hai final result (125) sahi (80) se kitna percent jyada hai. Value me jyada hai $125 - 80 = 45$. Base sahi value (80) rakh: $\frac{45}{80} \times 100 = \frac{9}{16} \times 100$. $\frac{1}{16}$ hota hai $6.25\%$, toh $9 \times 6.25 = 56.25\%$.

**Method 2 (Concept Builder):** Ratio method bhi op hai. Sahi value 80, galat 125. Ratio ban gaya $80:125 = 16:25$. Increase hai 9 units ka 16 par. Standard fraction $\frac{9}{16}$ aa gaya seedha!

**Exam Takeaway:** "More than the correct value" likha hai matlab percentage error original number (100) par nahi, balki 'Correct Outcome' (80) par nikalni padegi.

Action StateScale Value
A. Correct Value (Should be)1. $100 \rightarrow 80$
B. Mistaken Value (Actual)2. $100 \rightarrow 125$

questions_hin.q_hi: After three successive raises, Aftab's salary became equal to $\frac{378}{125}$ times of his initial salary. By what percentage was the salary raised the first time if the third raise was twice as high (in percentage) as the second raise and the second raise was twice as high (in percentage) as the first raise?
questions_hin.s_hi:
**Core Conceptual Tool:** 2. Successive Change (The Chain Reaction)

**Pen-Free Observation:** Dekh bhai, ye question agar x maan ke karega toh ek cubic equation ($x(2x)(4x)$...) ban jayegi aur tu wahin fans jayega. Fraction diya hai $\frac{378}{125} = 3.024$ ka multiplier. Options ko verify karna hi exam nikalne ka shortcut hai.

**Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):** Options try kar. Agar pehla raise 20\% hai, toh dusra uska double (40\%) aur teesra uska double (80\%). Inka successive lagao: $(1.2) \times (1.4) \times (1.8)$. Check kar: $1.2 \times 1.4 = 1.68$, and $1.68 \times 1.8 = 3.024$. Match kar gaya! Pehla option hi answer ho gaya.

**Method 2 (Concept Builder):** Conceptually, $\frac{378}{125}$ approx 3 times growth hai. Agar pehla 10\% lega (Op D), toh 1.1x1.2x1.4 = 1.84 banega jo bahut chhota hai. Agar 25\% (Op C) lega toh 1.25x1.5x2.0 = 3.75 banega jo bada ho jayega. Range definition (approximation) se bhi answer nikal aata.

**Exam Takeaway:** Successive change me agar multiplier weird decimal ya bada fraction ho aur multiple unknown changes pooche hon, HAMESHA reverse options elimination ka sahara liya kar.

questions_hin.q_hi: A man's annual income has increased by 5000 but the tax on income that he has to pay has reduced from 15% to 12%. While in both the situations, 30% of the income tax is tax-free. Find the initial income, if equal tax is paid in both cases?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: CPR (Constant Product Ratio)

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Tax = Income $\times$ Tax Rate. Jab Tax (Product) constant hai, toh Income aur Tax Rate inversely proportional honge. Rate 15 se 12 hua (Ratio 5:4). Toh Income 4 se 5 hui hogi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Tax free portion (30%) dono taraf cut jayega, ignore kar. Tax rate ratio = 15:12 = 5:4. CPR lagao: Tax same hai toh Income ratio = 4:5. Gap 1 unit ka hai. 1 unit = 5000 (increase). Toh initial income 4 units = 20000. Pen nahi uthana tha isme!

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Equation: $70\% \text{ of } 15\% \text{ of } x = 70\% \text{ of } 12\% \text{ of } (x + 5000)$. $15x = 12x + 60000 \implies 3x = 60000 \implies x = 20000$.

Future Exam Takeaway: CPR method CGL Mains me aag laga dega! Product constant dekhte hi cross-ratio lagao.

questions_hin.q_hi: Entry ticket of a cinema hall is 120 when the price is reduced by a certain percentage then the sales of ticket increases by 37.5%. whereas the overall collection is reduced by 25%. Find the percentage decrease in the price of ticket ?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: Cross-Product

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, ye basic equation hai $Price \times Sales = Collection$. Yaha ₹120 kisi kaam ka nahi hai kyuki result me percentage pucha hai. Collection ka aur Sales ka ratio banega, aur directly divide karke Price ka ratio niklega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Dependent variable (Collection) ko independent variables (Sales) se divide kar, Price nikal.

Mathematically :-
$$P = \frac{Collection}{Sales} \\\\ P_{ratio} = \frac{C_1}{S_1} : \frac{C_2}{S_2} = \frac{4}{8} : \frac{3}{11} = \frac{1}{2} : \frac{3}{11} \\\\ Cross \ Multiply \Rightarrow 11 : 6 \\\\ \% \ Decrease = \frac{11 - 6}{11} \times 100 = \frac{5}{11} \times 100 = 45.45\%$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Actual ₹120 le kar math solve kar, end me percent nikalo.

Mathematically :-
$$P_1 = 120, S_1 = 8x \Rightarrow C_1 = 960x \\\\ C_2 = 960x \times 0.75 = 720x \\\\ S_2 = 8x \times 1.375 = 11x \\\\ P_2 = \frac{720x}{11x} \approx 65.45 \\\\ \% \ Decrease = \frac{120 - 65.45}{120} \times 100 = 45.45\%$$

Exam Takeaway: Absolute values are completely useless if the question asks for a percentage output. Ignore them.

Multiplier EffectDivide final ratio by one shift ratio to get the other shift ratio.

questions_hin.q_hi: x is inversely proportional to y. If x is increased by $37.5\%$ then find % change in the value of y?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: 1. CPR (Constant Product Ratio)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, $x$ aur $y$ inversely proportional hain, iska matlab unka product $x \times y = K$ constant hai. Direct CPR shift lagega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): $37.5\%$ ki fraction $3/8$ hoti hai. X me increase hua $+3/8$. Toh CPR shift me Y decrease hoga $-3/(8+3) = -3/11$. $1/11$ hota hai $9.09\%$, toh $3/11$ banega $27.27\%$. Aankhon hi aankhon me answer!

Mathematically :-
$X_{inc} = +\frac{3}{8}$
$Y_{dec} = -\frac{3}{11}$
$\% = \frac{3}{11} \times 100 = 27.27\%$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Ratio se dekh le. $x$ agar 8 se 11 hua, toh inverse relation me $y$ 11 se 8 hoga. 3 ghata 11 par. Baakhi kahani same hai.

Mathematically :-
$xy = k$
$X_{new} = \frac{11}{8}x$
$Y_{new} = \frac{k}{\frac{11}{8}x} = \frac{8}{11}y$
$\text{Dec} = y - \frac{8}{11}y = \frac{3}{11}y$
$\% = \frac{3}{11} \times 100 = 27.27\%$

Exam Takeaway: Inversely proportional bolne ka matlab hi CPR lagana hai, fractions yaad hone chahiye tips par.

VariableShift
X (Increase)$+3/8$
Y (Decrease)$-3/11$

questions_hin.q_hi: If a number is first increased by 15%, then reduced by 15%, it results in 782. If the same number is first reduced by 25%, then increased by 25% and again reduced by 20%, then what will be the resulting number?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, same percentage increase/decrease hamesha $(x^2/100)\%$ ka loss deta hai. $15\%$ se $2.25\%$ loss yani 97.75% of number 782 hai. Decimal adjust kar number 800 aaya. Fir aage seedha fractions ko chain me kaat de.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): First setup se number extract kar aur second me purely fractions apply kar.

Mathematically :-
$$Loss = \frac{15^2}{100} = 2.25\% \\\\ 97.75\% \ of \ N = 782 \Rightarrow N = 800 \\\\ Final = 800 \times \frac{3}{4} \times \frac{5}{4} \times \frac{4}{5} \\\\ Final = 800 \times \frac{3}{4} = 600$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Decimal chain ko har step par equate kar.

Mathematically :-
$$N \times 1.15 \times 0.85 = 782 \\\\ N = \frac{782}{0.9775} = 800 \\\\ Ans = 800 \times 0.75 \times 1.25 \times 0.80 \\\\ Ans = 600 \times 1.25 \times 0.80 = 600$$

Exam Takeaway: Chain rule me fractions last tak cancel hone ke liye wait karti hain, intermediate gunna-bhag me time waste na karo.

List IList II
Constant Change Rule$+A\%, -A\% \Rightarrow Net \ Loss \ (A^2/100)\%$

questions_hin.q_hi: The salary of a person is ₹30,000. It increases first by $2k\%$ and then again by $k\%$, making his new salary ₹44,850. If his original salary was instead decreased by $2k\%$ and then further decreased by $k\%$, what would his new salary be?
questions_hin.s_hi:
The "Pen-Free" Observation First:

Dekh bhai, Final / Initial = $\frac{44850}{30000} = 1.495$. Matlab lagbhag $50\%$ ka growth hua hai successive me. Equation mat bana, Hit and trial best hai. $k=15$ lo, toh $+30\%$ aur $+15\%$ ka net lagbhag $49.5\%$ fit baith gaya!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Net Increase} = \frac{44850 - 30000}{30000} = 49.5\% \\ 2k + k + \frac{2k^2}{100} = 49.5 \implies k = 15 \text{ (by Observation)} \\ \text{Decrease } 1 = 30000 \times (1 - 0.30) = 21000 \\ \text{Decrease } 2 = 21000 \times (1 - 0.15) = 17850 $$

Exam Takeaway: Successive increase/decrease me agar exact formula lagane bethe toh quadratic banegi. Smart assumption + Hit & Trial rules the exam!

questions_hin.q_hi: In the year 2014, the population of a city was 30,000. The population of the city increased in 2015, 2016 and 2017 by a constant number. In the year 2018, if the population of the city was increased by 20% over the previous year then the population of the city become 27600 more than that of the year 2014. What is the ratio of the percentage increase in the population of the city over the previous year in the year 2015 to that in the year 2017 over the previous year?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, "constant number" matlab AP chal rahi hai. 2018 ki population $2014 + 27600$ se aayegi, phir $20\%$ back karke 2017 ka pata chalega. Reverse calculations kar mentally.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Reverse series laga aur yearly increase nikal. Mathematically :-

$P_{2018} = 30000 + 27600 = 57600$

$P_{2017} = \frac{57600}{1.2} = 48000$

$\text{Inc in 3 yrs} = 48000 - 30000 = 18000 \Rightarrow \text{6000 per yr}$

$\%_{2015} = \frac{6000}{30000} = \frac{1}{5}$

$\%_{2017} = \frac{6000}{42000} = \frac{1}{7}$

$\text{Ratio} = \frac{1}{5} : \frac{1}{7} = 7 : 5$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Variables assume karke AP ka formula chalao. Mathematically :-

$P_{2014} = 30000$

$P_{2017} = 30000 + 3d$

$(30000 + 3d) \times 1.2 = 57600$

$30000 + 3d = 48000 \Rightarrow 3d = 18000 \Rightarrow d = 6000$

$\frac{6000}{30000} : \frac{6000}{30000+2(6000)} = \frac{1}{5} : \frac{1}{7} = 7:5$

Exam Takeaway: Constant increase humesha Arithmetic Progression (AP) hota hai, pichhe se backward aana smart move hai.

List IList II
AP Logic$\text{Value} = a + (n-1)d$
